question: Do previously selected decoding recipes generalize to separate Stringer-coauthored visual-cortex recordings?
recording_rule: Earliest dated visual recording per published mouse ID; same-day block order is numeric
primary_regime: Fit each mouse independently; compare mouse means across three fixed training seeds. Models never see another new mouse in this regime.
secondary_regime: Jointly fit seven recording-specific read-ins/session embeddings and shared backbone; descriptive only because shared fitting induces dependence.
budget_derivation: 3 recipes x 3 seeds x (7 independent mice + 1 shared cohort) =72; no conditional extension
eligibility: Finite training-prefix values and training-prefix population SD >1e-6; random panel, sorted original neuron indices; no labels/positions in selection
activity_scaling: Per-neuron mean and population SD using the entire chronological training prefix only; floor SD1e-6
input: Only published spks; 32 native frames ending at target index, neuron identity implicit in read-in weights, no coordinates or past behavior
alignment: Same published activity/run indices over their common prefix; permit only absolute length difference<=1 and record discarded terminal index. No shifts, interpolation, learned lags, or timestamp-derived seconds. Author fig4 indexes run by the original neural itest indices. Raw sensor synchronization is inherited, not reconstructed.
target: abs(published run), as plotted by authors; physical speed units not asserted

splits.rule: floor fraction*N boundaries; validation/test start boundary+64; all windows remain entirely in their segment; targets start segment_start+63

train_example_rule: All eligible target indices if <=4096; otherwise integer linspace from first to last training target, unique and ordered, same endpoints for all models/histories. Fixed computation budget, not outcome-based subsampling.
validation_test_examples: All common eligible target times, no subsampling
label_scaling: Mean/SD of selected training targets only, floor1e-6; store float64 evaluation targets and float32 training labels
prediction_rule: Clamp standardized output at standardized zero speed; same for all algorithms. Raw metrics secondary.
checkpoint_selection: Earliest epoch minimizing clamped validation MSE including epoch0; shared score is equal-mouse mean MSE/max(validation training-mean MSE,0.05). No architecture/recipe selection on this cohort.
optimization: AdamW per fixed recipe, batch64, cosine to 0.1*lr, gradient norm clip1; full epochs, equal-mouse weighting for shared; same per-mouse permutation across paired recipes/regimes

ridge.definition: Standardize every flattened lag-feature using selected training examples; intercept unpenalized; minimize mean squared error + lambda*||w||^2; choose earliest sorted history/lambda with smallest clamped validation MSE

primary_metric: Mean across seven mice of 1 - mean_seed_candidate_test_MSE / mean_seed_comparator_test_MSE; each mouse equal weight; no pooling windows/seeds into animal count
statistics: Two-sided exact sign tests on seven non-tied independent-fit mouse mean-MSE differences, Holm correction across three prespecified contrasts at alpha0.05; direction reported symmetrically. Validity conditional on distinct animals, common-lab convenience sampling, fixed algorithms and independence assumption. Seeds/windows not independent biological replicates.
claim_rule: Report statistical and practical gates separately; require both plus beat training-mean control in all mouse means for a validated advantage in this cohort. No universal optimality, attention-specific mechanism, zero-shot transfer, forecasting, physical-causal or generation claim.
secondary_endpoints: all three seeds and epoch0 learning
evaluation_lock: Save hashes of every chosen neural/ridge checkpoint before any test prediction, error or target distribution is inspected. No later refit/reselection.
missing_data: Stop for failed integrity, rank/axis mismatch, absolute spks/run length difference>1, selected-panel nonfinite values, fewer than512 eligible cells, no varying training target or insufficient split examples. For a one-frame mismatch use common valid indices; never impute missing targets or choose alignment from model results.
limitations: one recording per mouse; one lab and visual cortex
same dataset lineage and publisher version2 deconvolution differs from original2019 data
new within-recording training required; not zero-shot transfer
native frame history retained; physical duration equivalence unverified
512 random cells; one fixed panel per mouse
comparison of independently optimized recipes does not isolate attention causally
timestamp discrepancy and original running preprocessing not independently reconstructed

amendment.reason: TX56 has29618 activity frames and29617 running entries. Authors use run[itest] with neural test indices; a common valid index domain preserves that source convention. Original guard stopped successfully. No performance/target-distribution inspection or new fits occurred.
amendment.data_before_amendment: TX57 prepared under identical-index rule; training-only statistics saved. No validation/test performance or distributions inspected. TX56 headers only.
amendment.interpretation: Index-domain restriction is an explicit source-supported convention, not proof of raw sensor timing or cause of the mismatch.
